about: How a seat is said inside a sentence (Fable B's ruling, Nov 11, on #8750): a seat on a body by the body ("run for the Mutual Village Council", then "the council"), a single office by its title in lower case ("run for mayor"), a district's seat with its district. Read by seatSaid in src/english/journal-words.ts. `address` is how a resident hails an official by office and family name ("Commissioner McGee"; Fable B's street stop, Nov 11), matched on the office's title; an office with no form here is hailed by first name.
